name: Week 29 Optional KB — Bent Press Flow + B-Stance Flow
description:
**Optional — take it whenever a window opens.** The three gym days complete the week; this is a bonus, not a debt.

**The Bent Press Flow comes back as the anchor** after a stretch away, and **the B-stance flow returns** for the offset-stance work that has not appeared in months. Both are skill work — keep the bell light and unhurried. One round of each is a complete session on a bad-sleep day.

dayOverview.theme: Two canonical flows and one maintenance strength round. Written short and optional — run two rounds of each when fresh, one when the night was bad, and either version counts as done.

spotlights.why: The bent press is the move that has quietly gone missing from this program before. It is a skill lift, not a strength lift — go light and spend the attention on the hip drive and the eyes staying on the bell.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W30 — Leggy Flow and the kickstand complex come back around. W31 — figure-8 → tactical clean if it has not appeared by then.
watchpoints: 🛑 keep it shy — the cue is the cap: bent press, snatch, overhead lunge, all the cleans, the KB strict press. Overhead and ballistic work where the cue breaking is the ceiling.
🔥 near-failure last set OK: KB curl. Nothing else here is a lift to chase.
**Banded shoulder prep is a KB-day anchor.** It stays even on a twenty-minute version of this session.
**The bent press is a skill, not a load.** Light bell. If the eyes leave the bell or the hip stops driving, the set is over.
**KB curl, left arm first.** Twice a week is the dose — frequency for the left side, not intensity.
**Week three of the newborn.** One round of each flow is a complete session. Missing this day entirely does not make the week incomplete.

sets.name: Warm-Up — Halos + Cossacks + Around-the-Body (Light Bell)
sets.notes:
Light bell throughout. The cossacks double as an early-warning system — how they feel tells you what kind of session this is, and that read has been more reliable than sleep quality.

**Tired-day version:** 5 reps each.

exercises.notes: Light bell. Hand-eye primer — and a favourite, so enjoy it.
Close to the head, elbows leading. Opens the shoulders without loading them.
**Your readiness screen.** Deep as the hips allow, heel down. Read it against your own normal — the old ankle sprain means a stiff day here is not a forecast.
Deep core before the bell gets heavy.
**Protective activation.** A bell in each hand works if no DBs are around. Straight up, squeeze, slow release.

sets.name: Banded Shoulder Prep (~2 min)
sets.notes:
One round of all seven, about two minutes. Sustained tension, no rest between positions. **This is the KB-day shoulder anchor and it does not come out** — it is a large part of why the right shoulder has stayed quiet through a heavy block.

**Tired-day version:** 6 reps each. Exhausted: do it anyway at whatever range is smooth.

exercises.notes: Arms overhead, pull apart without letting the ribs flare.
Slow and controlled. Blades down and together.
Thumbs up, arms to a T. Traps stay quiet.
Rear delts. Lead with the elbows.
Hold the V overhead. Ribs down, shoulders packed.

sets.name: 🌀 Bent Press Flow — Back as the Anchor
sets.notes:
**Light bell — 25-35.** Two rounds each side when fresh, one when tired.

This is the program's oldest flow and it is skill work first. **Run it as one continuous chain**, not five separate exercises: the transitions are the part worth practising. 🛑 The bent press caps the bell — if the hip stops driving or the eyes leave the bell, the flow drops a size.

sets.name: Strength — KB Row + Strict Press + Curl 🛑
sets.notes:
Run this between the two flows so the demanding work is not all stacked at the end.

**Tired-day version:** one round.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD: 50.** Maintenance — the real row volume lives on pull day. 50 being easy is the correct end state; do not chase it.
- Flat back, elbow past the ribs
- Slow eccentric, full stretch at the bottom

**LOAD: 50, strict — clean to rack, press straight up, no push-press.** 50 is the Arrilaga ceiling, so the pause is the progression.
- **2-3s PAUSE AT LOCKOUT every rep** — bicep by the ear, shoulder packed **DOWN**, ribs down, and hold it
- Full lockout before the count starts — no soft elbow
- Both sides to the same standard

**LOAD: light bell, ~25-35. LEFT ARM FIRST — match the right to it.**
- **Upper arm pinned to the ribs**, elbow does not drift forward
- **Slow lower to a full stretch** — the bell loads the bottom where a dumbbell goes slack
- Shoulder packed down, no shrug to start

🔥 Near-failure fine on the last set. Twice a week is the dose — this is frequency for the left arm, not intensity.

sets.name: 🌀 B-Stance Flow — Returns After a Long Gap
sets.notes:
**Light to moderate bell.** Two rounds each side when fresh, one when tired.

The offset stance is the whole point — it makes every beat an anti-rotation exercise without adding load. 🛑 Keep the snatch clean; if it stops being clean, the flow is over rather than the bell getting heavier.

sets.name: Cooldown (Hip + Shoulder Release)
sets.notes:
The flows were lunge-heavy and finished overhead. Give both the hips and the shoulders a beat.

**Tired-day version:** 30s each.

exercises.notes: 30s each arm, elbow at MID height.
Passive decompression after the overhead work.
45s each side. The lunges earned this.

tips: Optional means optional. One round of each flow is a complete session.
Light bell on the bent press — it is a skill lift, not a strength lift.
KB curl left arm first, and the left sets the reps.
Banded prep stays even on the short version.
